newsitem.title: FINLAND: SOP says pulp options trade picking up.
newsitem.headline: SOP says pulp options trade picking up.

text.p: Trade in pulp derivatives on Finnish futures and options exchange Suomen Optioporssi Oy (SOP) is picking up after a quiet start to the year, the exchange's CEO, Anders Lindeberg, said on Monday.
Swedish options exchange OM Gruppens said in February it would open a pulp derivatives exchange on May 29.

"On the whole, trade in the early part of the year was quiet, but demand has been picking up lately. And that could be related to the fact that prices are changing," Lindeberg told Reuters by telephone.

"Prices have been rising for about the past two weeks," he said. On Monday, SOP put the latest value of its PIX pulp index for northern bleached softwood pulp at $542.66 per tonne, up from $524.55 a week ago.
Lindeberg said about 150 contracts had been traded on the exchange since it started up in February.

Deals usually come in batches of 10 to 30 contracts, he said. On Monday morning, 30 contracts were traded on the exchange's June future contract at $540.00 per tonne, in a bid-ask spread of $538.00 to $545.00.

Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy, reporting on its first quarter, said on Monday market pulp producers had curtailed production as they entered the second quarter so prices would rise before the summer.
But it warned that the later part of the year might see growth in production and over-supply.
At the end of April, Swedish forestry group Modo said it was optimistic about plans to hike pulp prices to $580 per tonne in May.
Swedish cooperative group Sodra said that the first quarter looked like a turning point for hitherto weak pulp prices.
